accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.intro: Each number of the application has a source and an accuracy limit. This screen shows the measured errors of the engine and the items that have no check.

self.title: Checks on this computer
self.intro: These checks calculate the values again in this browser and compare them with reference values. The reference values come from JPL Horizons, from exact solutions, or from definitions.
self.fast: The application does the checks of positions, time, frames and propagation.
self.flight: The application calculates the flight of {craft}.
self.good: All {n} checks are in their limits.
self.bad: {n} checks are not in their limits.
self.failed: The checks stopped because of an error.

tests.title: Results of the automatic tests ({n} checks)
tests.intro: These results are from the tests before the release of this version. Each row is the largest error that a test measured. If an error is larger than the test limit, the test result is a failure.

unverified.title: Items with no check
unverified.intro: These items have no comparison with an independent reference. Use them with caution.

limits.title: Limits of the models
limits.intro: The engine has no model for these effects.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: These are the technical names that the application uses.

self.time: Time of J2000 from the UTC date
self.hohmann: Hohmann transfer from the Lambert solver
self.integrator: Integrator: 10 revolutions of an eccentric orbit
self.flightVinf: {craft}, calculated flight: speed at infinity at {body}
self.flightPeriapsis: {craft}, calculated flight: radius of the closest approach to {body}

outerCenters.title: Centers of Uranus and Neptune
outerCenters.text: The barycenters of the two planet systems agree with JPL Horizons to 0.003 km. The application calculates each planet center from the barycenter and the moon model. The JPL Horizons centers are 4 811 km (Uranus) and 2 208 km (Neptune) from these results. The moons cannot move the planet that far. A possible cause is that Horizons uses satellite ephemeris files with a different barycenter. There is no check of this cause.

rotation.title: Rotation angle of the bodies
rotation.text: The application uses the pole and the rotation rate of the NAIF file pck00011.tpc to show the maps of the bodies. No test compares the rotation angle with a reference. The trajectory calculations do not use the rotation angle. They use the pole direction for the J2 force.

otherTools.title: Files in other programs
otherTools.text: The file writers obey the format documents of CCSDS, STK and GMAT. The tests read the files again with the readers of this application. No test opened the files in STK or in GMAT, because these programs were not available.

ste.title: Simplified Technical English
ste.text: A script examined the texts of the application with the writing rules of ASD-STE100 and a word list. The script does not have the official dictionary of the specification.

masses.title: Spacecraft masses
masses.text: The masses and the specific impulse of each spacecraft are example values. They are not the values of the actual spacecraft.

insertionBurns.title: Insertion burns of Cassini and Juno
insertionBurns.text: The application calculates each insertion burn as an impulse that gives the orbit of the JPL trajectory after the burn. No test compares the size of the burn with a published value.

models3d.title: Dimensions of the spacecraft models
models3d.text: The 3D models obey published dimensions where a source was available. The dimensions of the models of the Mars 2020 cruise stage and of Ulysses are estimates.

browsers.title: Other browsers and computers
browsers.text: The check of the pictures of the screens was in one browser on one computer. The check for a small screen used a browser window with the size of a phone screen: no check used an actual phone. The engine tests used Node.js. The checks on this screen show if your browser gives the same numbers.

maneuverSearch.title: Maneuvers that the search finds in a table
maneuverSearch.text: The Files screen finds velocity changes in a trajectory table. For the deep-space maneuver of Cassini, the size and the time agree with the velocity change in the JPL Horizons table. No test compares the results with the maneuver documents of a mission.

pictures.title: Colors and brightness of the bodies in the 3D view
pictures.text: The maps come from mission data. The brightness of each map and the values of each atmosphere do not come from measured data: the project set them for a good picture. No test compares the pictures with images from spacecraft or telescopes. The source of the Jupiter map does not give the longitude of the map. Thus the 3D view can show the clouds of Jupiter at an incorrect longitude.

smallShapes.title: Shapes of the small bodies in the 3D view
smallShapes.text: The shape of an asteroid or a comet in the 3D view is approximate: it shows the type of the shape, not a measured model. A body with no radius in the JPL Small-Body Database has a radius of 10 km in the picture.

impulses.title: Burns are impulses
impulses.text: Each maneuver changes the velocity in zero time. A long burn of an actual engine has losses that the model does not include.

forces.title: Forces of the model
forces.text: The force model has point-mass gravity, the J2 of the planets and the relativity term of the Sun. If you set it, the model also has radiation pressure on a sphere. It has no atmosphere, no higher gravity terms and no attitude.

moons.title: Moons
moons.text: The moon positions come from an analytic model with errors of 83 km to 41 400 km. A plan can use the flyby of a planet. It cannot give an accurate flyby of a moon.

launch.title: Launch
launch.text: A flight starts in a circular parking orbit. The model does not include the launch site or the flight from the ground to the orbit.

entry.title: Atmosphere entry
entry.text: A flight with an entry stops at the equatorial radius of the body. The model does not include the atmosphere.

interpolation.title: Interpolation
interpolation.text: Between the steps of the integrator, the positions come from an interpolation. For the flight of Voyager 2, the largest interpolation error that the test measured is 0.06 km.

range.title: Date range
range.text: The planet data is for 1950 to 2100. The small-body data is for 1980 to 2060.

centralBody.title: Plans around the Sun only
centralBody.text: A plan is a sequence of transfers around the Sun with flybys. The application cannot make a plan around a planet, for example a tour of the moons of Jupiter. After an arrival burn, a flight can stay in an orbit around the planet.

utcBefore1972.title: UTC before 1972
utcBefore1972.text: UTC has leap seconds from 1972. For a date before 1972, the application uses TAI − UTC = 9 s. This is not the UTC of those years: the error of a UTC time before 1972 can be some seconds. This limit does not change the TDB times.

lightTime.title: No light time
lightTime.text: All positions are geometric positions at one time. The application does not correct a position for the time of the light between a body and the point of view.
